newsitem.title: UK: Burmah gains as results beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Burmah gains as results beat forecasts.

text.p: Shares in Burmah Castrol Plc rose in early trading on Monday after better-than-expected 1996 results from the lubricants group.
The stock -- which touched an eight-month low of 976p on March 21 -- was up 9p at 10.06-1/2 stg by 0737 GMT in thin trade of 29,014 shares.

"The results were rather better than could have been hoped and have gone down very well," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "The 13 percent underlying improvement in profits was very respectable."

Burmah posted a rise in profits before exceptional items to 148.7 million stg -- compared with forecasts mostly in a range between 139.5 million stg and 141.5 million -- up 13 percent at constant exchange rates.

The company said trading conditions in 1996 showed little change through the year, with strong growth in Asia Pacific and other developing regions offset by more diffucult conditions in Europe and North America.
Chairman Lawrence Urquhart said continued strength in the pound would bear down on profits in the current year while market conditions were unlikely to show much change from 1996.
